name: Lexical Variance Profiling
description: Measures statistical deviations in token length to detect artificially uniform reading flows.
mechanism: Human writing exhibits high variance in word length distribution due to cognitive linguistic choices, contextual nuance, and natural vocabulary constraints. Conversely, LLMs tend to converge on a highly uniform, optimized median word length derived from their training corpus and subword tokenization biases (such as BPE). By measuring the statistical standard deviation in average word length across local text windows, this method pinpoints the unnaturally consistent lexical cadences that signify auto-regressive machine generation.
parameters:
Analysis: Lexical statistics
Metric: Token Standard Deviation
Output: 0-100 Homogeneity Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 65-85% standalone accuracy. Performance increases significantly when combined with complementary text analysis methods. Results vary with text length, language, and content type.
source: Statistical NLP analysis methods for AI-generated text detection. Based on computational linguistics and information theory research.
useCase: Detecting AI text that maintains an artificially 'smooth' reading rhythm by avoiding natural human vocabulary fluctuations.
strengths:
• Highly resistant to simple prompt engineering without strict lexical constraints.
• Fast, deterministic calculation with minimal computational overhead.
• Operates purely on lexical surface features, circumventing semantic obfuscation.
limitations:
• Heavily skewed by technical documents or academic journals which naturally feature longer vocabulary.
• Ineffective on short text excerpts (<100 words).
• Non-native speakers may naturally mimic this tight word length distribution.

references.title: Yule, G.U. (1944). The Statistical Study of Literary Vocabulary. Cambridge University Press.
Manning, C.D. & Schütze, H. (1999). Foundations of Statistical Natural Language Processing. MIT Press.
